initial_observation.encounter_context: admitted to the hospital with complaints related to abdominal lump and pain
initial_observation.chief_complaint: a lump and pain in the abdomen for the last two months associated with on and off fever with chills
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: The patient had abdominal lump and pain for two months with intermittent fever and chills; past medical history insignificant; denied recent infections, sexual activities or vaginal discharge; last menstrual period one month before; BMI 24.5; vital signs steady; pallor present; breast and systemic examinations normal; no diabetes; serology for HBsAg, HCV and HIV negative; laboratory tests including hemogram, liver and renal function, tumor markers normal; abdomen soft but tender; vaginal exam found left lower abdomen mass 10x8.5 cm.
presenting_symptoms: on and off fever with chills

evidence_items.source_text: The contrast enhanced tomography (CECT) of the whole abdomen showed a heterogeneous enhancing solid cystic lesion with septations measuring 10x9.5x9.0 cm in the left ovary (Figure 1A).

Gross findings of the left ovary specimen were showing a mass measuring 11 x 9.0 x 8.5 cm. The fallopian tube measured 4.5 cm in length. The outer surface of the ovary mass was encapsulated and light yellow serous fluid was seen oozing upon the incision. The cut surface of the incised mass showed cystic and solid areas with interspersed black pigmentation (Figure 1B).

The Hematoxylin and Eosin (HE) and Periodic acid Schiff (PAS) stained sections of the ovarian mass were showing dense inflammation, and necrosis. They were having florid fungal septate hyphae with dichotomous branching and was diagnosed as ovarian Aspergillosis (Figures 1C-E). The microscopy of sections from the left fallopian tube showed unremarkable histology (Figure 1F).
After a diagnosis of ovarian aspergillosis, the patient was given an intravenous formulation of voriconazole (6 mg/kg/day) and liposomal amphotericin B (0.5 mg/kg/day) for a period of ten days.
In retrospect, a CECT of the thorax was suggested to rule out focus in the respiratory tract, which revealed no abnormality.
